items.claim: The reportable bar for request smuggling is a cross-user consequence — bypassing security controls, reaching sensitive data, or directly compromising other application users — rather than a parsing discrepancy on its own.
items.body:
The reportable bar for request smuggling is a cross-user consequence — bypassing security controls, reaching sensitive data, or directly compromising other application users — rather than a parsing discrepancy on its own.

HackTricks reference: http desync (https://kathan19.gitbook.io/howtohunt/http-desync-attack/http_desync.md)
items.disproof: Front-end and back-end agree on the framing of the malformed request, so it is rejected consistently and no other application user's request is affected.

sources.quote: Request smuggling vulnerabilities are often critical in nature, allowing an attacker to bypass security controls, gain unauthorized access to sensitive data, and directly compromise other application users.

If a Transfer-Encoding header field is present in a request and the chunked transfer coding is not the final encoding, the message body length cannot be determined reliably; the server MUST respond with the 400 (Bad Request) status code and then close the connection.

For example, discrepancies can arise in how to handle duplicate headers like two Transfer-encoding (TE) or two Content-length (CL), or the malicious HTTP message will have different headers for TE and CL.
